name: vix_spike_mean_reversion_5s
author: adapted from Gemini Quant
thesis: Exploits 'Volatility Overpricing'. A sudden 5% spike in India VIX within 10 minutes often leads to an over-reaction in Nifty 50 component prices. As VIX stabilizes, the delta-hedging pressure from option writers subsides, leading to a quick price recovery. This is a market microstructure constraint.
mechanism: VIX spikes represent fear premium overshooting. As the initial shock is absorbed, options market makers delta-hedge their short puts by buying the underlying, creating upward pressure on spot. The mean-reverting nature of implied volatility means the fear premium decays rapidly, pulling spot higher within minutes to hours.
weaknesses: VIX spikes can lead to sustained crashes (regime change)
Slippage is high during high VIX
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
